questions.q: What does the ON clause in a JOIN specify?
options: The predicate that decides which rows from each table get paired together
The columns to display in the results
The sort order of the final results
Which database to connect to
questions.explain: ON works just like a WHERE predicate (Lesson 20), but specifically determines row pairing across the two tables.

questions.q: What does INNER JOIN do with a row that has no match on the other table?
options: It's dropped from the result entirely
It's included with NULLs filling in for the missing side
It causes an error
It's duplicated for every row in the other table
questions.explain: INNER JOIN only returns rows where the ON condition matches on both sides — unmatched rows on either side disappear.

questions.q: Why do you need table aliases once two joined tables share a column name?
options: You must qualify which table's column you mean (e.g. p.ProductID vs. sod.ProductID), and aliases make that shorter
Aliases are required syntax for every JOIN, regardless of column names
Aliases change which rows match in the ON clause
Without an alias, SQL Server picks one table's column arbitrarily
questions.explain: When both Production.Product and Sales.SalesOrderDetail have a ProductID column, an unqualified reference would be ambiguous.

questions.q: When does WHERE run relative to a JOIN?
options: After the join has already combined matching rows
Before the join, filtering each table separately first
WHERE cannot be used in a query that includes a JOIN
At the exact same time as the ON clause, with identical behavior
questions.explain: WHERE filters the already-joined, combined result set — this follows the same logical processing order established in Lesson 11.

questions.q: In 'FROM Production.Product AS p INNER JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod ON p.ProductID = sod.ProductID', what determines which rows appear together?
options: Rows where p.ProductID equals sod.ProductID
Every possible combination of rows from both tables
Only rows where p.Name equals sod.OrderQty
Rows are matched by their row number/position, not any column
questions.explain: The ON condition is the predicate deciding the match — here, equal ProductID values on both sides.
